newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks open slightly higher.
newsitem.headline: French stocks open slightly higher.

text.p: French shares opened slightly higher on Thursday, underpinned by the French bond market, but volume was limited ahead of a Bank of France policy council meeting today and a set of U.S. data due on Friday.
The French market will be closed on Friday for All Saints.

A record 12.6 percent September unemployment figure, released this morning, could add weigh to arguments for lower French rates but Britain's rate increase on Wednesday may point to the other direction.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 4.23 points or 0.2 percent at 2,128.99 at 0905 GMT.
The CAC-40 future was up five points at 2,129
Alcatel Alsthom, up 0.53 pct, sold its 2.2 percent stake in Lafarge, up 0.17 percent, to the company for 660 million francs.
Cie de Suez, down 0.32 percent, chief executive Gerard Mestrallet told a Belgian newspaper it was likely to sell Generale de Belgique's nine percent stake in Accor, up 0.95 percent.
Mestrallet said he had invited Belgian financier Albert Frere to boost his stake in the company to seven percent. Frere has been buying recently and is rumoured to hold five percent.
